I have a mental math test coming up for a quantitative trading firm. Anyone knows good websites to practice?

For mental math practice, Zetamac is widely considered the gold standard for quant trading interview prep. It generates randomized arithmetic problems (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and tracks your accuracy and speed. Many prop trading firms use similar tests, so practicing on Zetamac will directly translate to better performance on actual assessments.

RankBrain is another excellent resource that offers customizable difficulty levels and various problem types including percentages, squares, and cube roots. Arithmetic.zetamac.com and MentalMath.coach are also popular alternatives that simulate the timed format typical of trading firm assessments. These platforms help build both speed and accuracy under pressure.

item Trading firms often test mental math because traders need to make quick calculations under pressure. Beyond websites, try practicing with a friend quizzing you, or use mobile apps like Mental Math Master. For more comprehensive preparation, consider combining online practice with mental math techniques from books like "Secrets of Mental Math" by Arthur Benjamin. Consistency is key—aim for 15-20 minutes of daily practice rather than long cramming sessions.
